title: The geometric Frobenius fixes the unit class in degree-zero cohomology of the constant Weil sheaf
statement: Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$ and a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen algebraic closure $\Qlb$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme such that $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $(E_Y,\theta_E)\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ be the constant Weil sheaf with its canonical Weil structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], let $F:H^0(Y,E)\to H^0(Y,E)$ be the geometric Frobenius [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] of $(E_Y,\theta_E)$ in degree $0$, and let $1_E\in H^0(Y,E)$ be the unit class of [lem-pod-connected-constant-h0] (3). Then $F(1_E)=1_E$.

source.place: (1.11)-(1.12), pp. 277-278: the isomorphism F^*: F^*F -> F of a sheaf coming from X_0 is defined through the etale space, which for the constant sheaf is X x (constant set) with F^* the identity on constant sections; blueprint prop-cohomological-finiteness, ## Proof, Step 7 ('the Weil structure of the constant Weil sheaf is the identity on the constants'); written by an agent

proof.text: Put $B_n=(A_{E,n})_Y$. These are constructible sheaves in degree $0$ [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](1). Applying [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] to $R_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, whose derived reductions are $B_n$ by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2), gives $N_n=Ra_{Y*,n}B_n\in D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$. For this $N_n$, unfold [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]: $\tau_{B_n}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(e_n)\circ\iota_{N_n}$ with $e_n=\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(B_n)$. The map $e_n$ is the specified unit-square-counit mate, not a chosen base-change isomorphism [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1). The point map is restriction along $g_s$, colimit insertion, then $\kappa$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Apply [lem-pod-frobenius-exchange-degree-zero] to $M=B_n$: on $H^0$, $\iota$ sends $v$ to the inserted restriction of $v$, tensored with $1$; $e_n$ is the underived exchange mate, and multiplication $\lambda_n$ removes this tensor factor. Thus, with $p_{g_Y,B_n}$ the restriction--insertion pullback of sections, $$\Gamma(Y,\lambda_n)\,H^0(\tau_{B_n})=p_{g_Y,B_n}.$$ Exact sections on $s$ justify reading these maps on degree-zero sheaf cohomology [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

proof.text: Let $u_n$ denote the constant section with value $1\in A_{E,n}$, and put $U_n=H^0(\RGamma(c_n\lambda_n)\circ\tau_{B_n})$. By [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](1), $c_n$ is adjoint to the sheaf map $B_n\to g_{Y*}B_n$ sending each constant $b$ to the same constant $b$. Pulling back the constant section $b$ gives its restriction at $(Y\xrightarrow{g_Y}Y)$ and the corresponding colimit coprojection; applying this adjoint $c_n$ returns $b$. Hence $\Gamma(c_n)p_{g_Y,B_n}(u_n)=u_n$, and the formula in Step 1 gives $U_n(u_n)=u_n$. This computes the finite coefficient action; the Frobenius acts on the scheme, while $c_n$ leaves the coefficient value $1$ fixed. Moreover the stated reduction relation $(r_n)_Yc_{n+1}=c_ng_Y^{-1}((r_n)_Y)$ sends $u_{n+1}$ to $u_n$.

proof.text: Set $R_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $N=Ra_{Y*}R_Y$. The coefficient-object theorem gives $R_Y\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $R_Y\otimes^L A_{E,n}\cong B_n$ [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2). The morphism $a_Y:Y\to\Spec k$ is a finite-type $k$-morphism and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$, so [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] gives $N\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$, derived complete, with $N\otimes^L A_{E,n}\cong N_n$. This verifies the bounded constructible, derived-complete domain needed to apply the integral point-transport theorem. In particular [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-realization] identifies the SPECIFIED $\iota_N$ with the realization of the restriction--insertion--$x\mapsto x\otimes1$ maps $\iota_{N_n}$ on the coherent reduction tower. All these identifications use the actual completeness and projection maps.

proof.text: Write $c_R=(\varprojlim_nc_n)\circ\mathrm{comparison}$ and $\theta_R=c_R\lambda_R$ as in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](2),(3). The normalization [lem-pod-canonical-coefficient-pullback-reduction] gives $$\pi_n\theta_R=\operatorname{Res}_n(c_n\lambda_n)\rho_n.$$ Thus $\lambda_R$ is the multiplication/completeness comparison with the specified finite multiplication maps; no arbitrary identification of $Lg_Y^*R_Y$ with $g_Y^{-1}R_Y$ is substituted. The integral exchange of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1) is $\beta_*\mathcal L_s(e_{a_Y})\alpha_*$, formed on strict semilinear systems, whose finite evaluations are $e_n$. The operation comparisons preserve the square identification, units and counits [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Together with the point-transport realization of Step 3, this gives for the canonical cohomology projections $P_n:H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ and $U_R=H^0(\RGamma(\theta_R)\tau_{R_Y})$ the equation $$P_nU_R=U_nP_n.$$ Indeed, projecting the three arrows of $U_R$ in their order gives $\iota_{N_n}$, $\operatorname{Fib}_s(e_n)$, and $\RGamma(c_n\lambda_n)$, respectively. Naturality of the specified projection comparisons permits their composition, producing the displayed equation. These are compatible maps of whole systems, not a claim that individual reductions determine arbitrary derived morphisms.

proof.text: By [lem-pod-connected-constant-h0](2), $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to\varprojlim_n H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ given by the $P_n$ is an isomorphism and $P_n(1_{\mathcal O_E})=u_n$. Therefore for every $n$, $$P_n(U_R(1_{\mathcal O_E}))=U_n(u_n)=u_n=P_n(1_{\mathcal O_E}).$$ Injectivity of that inverse-limit isomorphism gives $U_R(1_{\mathcal O_E})=1_{\mathcal O_E}$. Only equality of degree-zero elements is detected here; no detection of equality of derived morphisms by projections is used.

proof.text: At the rational stage the constant structure is $\theta_E=\theta_R\otimes1$ [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](4). The point transport is explicitly $\iota_N^E=\iota_N^{\mathcal O_E}\otimes E$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], the exchange is the scalar localization of its integral mate [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1), and operation comparisons commute with rationalization [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Consequently the endomorphism $F=H^0(\RGamma(\theta_E)\circ\tau_{E_Y})$ specified by [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] is $U_R\otimes E$ on $H^0(Y,E)=H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\otimes E$. Clause (3) of [lem-pod-connected-constant-h0] identifies the distinguished unit as $1_E=1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$. Hence $$F(1_E)=(U_R\otimes E)(1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1)=U_R(1_{\mathcal O_E})\otimes1=1_E.$$
